 Judgment
Though this appeal is listed for orders, it is taken up for final disposal, with the consent of learned counsel for both the parties.

2. The claimants are before this Court praying for enhancement of compensation, not being satisfied with the compensation awarded under judgment and award dated 13.11.2019 passed in MVC No.1344/2018 on the file of learned Principal Senior Civil Judge and Member, Addl. MACT,
Belagavi (for short, 'Tribunal').
3.

The claimants, who are mother and brother of the deceased Sagar @ Shivaji Bhavaku Mutagekar,
filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 seeking compensation for the accidental death of deceased Sagar that took place on 10.06.2018 involving Motorcycle bearing Engine No.BGAI-390500 and Tipper bearing registration No.KA-22/C-1690.
It is stated that the deceased was aged 30 years as on the date of accident and he was doing centering and coolie work and earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
NC: 2023:KHC-D:7539-DB appeared through their learned counsel.
Respondent No.2- Insurance Company filed its statement of objections denying the allegations made in the claim petition.
It was contended that due to negligent riding of rider of motorcycle, accident took place.
It further contended that rider of motorcycle as well as driver of offending Tipper were not having valid and effective driving license as on the date of accident.
Thus, prayed for dismissal of the claim petition.
5. Before the Tribunal, 1st claimant-mother of the deceased was examined as PW1 apart from marking the documents as Exs.P1 to P10.

Respondent No.2-Insurer did not examine any witness,
but got marked insurance policy as Ex.R1.

The Tribunal based on the material evidence on record awarded total compensation of Rs.7,34,000/- with interest at 9% per annum on the following heads:
 Loss of Dependency Rs.7,14,000/-

2  Funeral expenses Rs. 10,000/-
 Loss of love & affection Rs. 10,000/-
 Total Rs.7,34,000/-
 NC: 2023:KHC-D:7539-DB 6.

While awarding the above compensation, Tribunal assessed notional income of the deceased at Rs.7,000/- per month, deducted 50% towards personal and living expenses of the deceased and applied multiplier of 17.
The claimants not being satisfied with quantum of compensation awarded by Tribunal are before this Court praying for enhancement of compensation.

7. Heard Sri. Nitin R Bolabandi, learned counsel for the appellants-claimants as well as Sri. G.N.
Raichur, learned counsel for the respondent-Insurance Company and perused the appeal papers along with original records.
8.

Sri.Nitin R Bolabandi, learned counsel for the appellants-claimants would submit that notional income of the deceased assessed by Tribunal at Rs.7,000/- per month is on the lower side, inasmuch as deceased was doing centering and coolie work and earning Rs.20,000/- per month.

He further submitted that in the light of decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Company NC: 2023:KHC-D:7539-DB Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi & Others1, the claimants would be entitled to an addition of 40% of the assessed income towards future prospects.

entities.text: National Insurance Company NC: 2023:KHC-D:7539-DB Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi & Others1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is his submission that no compensation has been awarded under conventional heads.
He submitted that as per decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Pranay Sethi (supra), the claimants would be entitled to Rs.15,000/- towards loss of estate and Rs.15,000/- towards funeral expenses.

It is further submitted that the Tribunal committed an error in not awarding compensation on the head of loss of consortium, which the 1st claimant-mother of the deceased would be entitled to Rs.40,000/- towards filial consortium as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Magma General Insurance Company Ltd., Vs. Nanu Ram and Others2.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Company Ltd., Vs. Nanu Ram and Others2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, he prays for allowing the appeal.

9. Per contra, Sri. G.N. Raichur, learned counsel appearing for the respondent-Insurance Company would contend that in the absence of any cogent or acceptable document to prove the avocation and income of the deceased, the Tribunal is justified in assessing notional AIR 2017 SC 5157 2018 ACJ 2782 NC: 2023:KHC-D:7539-DB income of the deceased at Rs.7,000/- per month, which is just and proper.

He further submits that the Tribunal on appreciation of the material on record awarded just and reasonable compensation under various heads, which does not call for any interference at the hands of this Court.
Thus, he prays for dismissal of the appeal.

10. Having heard the learned counsel for the parties and on perusal of the appeal papers including the original records, the only point that would fall for consideration in this appeal is, whether the claimants would be entitled for enhanced compensation?

sentences.text: Our answer to the above point is in the affirmative for the following reasons.

12. The occurrence of accident on 10.06.2018 involving Motorcycle bearing Engine No.BGAI-390500 and Tipper bearing registration No.KA-22/C-1690 and resultant death of deceased Sagar is not in dispute in this appeal.
It is the contention of appellants-claimants that notional income of the deceased assessed by the Tribunal at Rs.7,000/- per month is on the lower side.
The claimants in order to prove NC: 2023:KHC-D:7539-DB the avocation and earning of the deceased have not produced any cogent or acceptable document.

In the absence of any documentary evidence to establish the avocation and income of the deceased, this Court and Lok Adalath while settling the accidental claims of the year 2018, would normally assess notional income at Rs.11,750/-
per month, taking note of the chart prepared by KSLSA based on various factors including the minimum wage fixed.

Therefore, in the instant case also, in the absence of any corroborative document to establish the income of the deceased, we are of the opinion that it would be just and appropriate to determine notional income of the deceased at Rs.11,750/- p.m., taking note of the income chart prepared by KSLSA and also the minimum wage fixed.
13. Further, the Tribunal committed an error in not adding 40% of the assessed income towards future prospects of the deceased.

In the case of Pranay Sethi (supra), the Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that wherever the deceased was aged below 40 years, the claimants would be entitled for addition of 40% of the assessed income NC: 2023:KHC-D:7539-DB towards future prospects.
In the instant case, the deceased was aged 30 years.
Therefore, the claimants would be entitled for addition of 40% of the assessed income towards future prospects.
Since the deceased was a bachelor

,
deduction of 50% taken by the Tribunal towards personal and living expenses of the deceased is just and proper and same is not disturbed.
Proper multiplier applicable to the age of the deceased is '17'.

Thus, the claimants would be entitled for compensation on the head of loss of dependency at Rs.16,77,900/- (Rs.11,750 + 40% x 12 x 17 x 1/2).
14.

It is well settled law that the 1st claimant being mother of the deceased would be entitled to Rs.40,000/- towards filial consortium as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. (supra).

As held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Pranay Sethi (supra), the claimants would be entitled to Rs.15,000/- towards loss of estate, besides Rs.15,000/-
towards transportation of dead body and funeral expenses.

Thus, claimants would be entitled for modified compensation on the following heads:
NC: 2023:KHC-D:7539-DB Sl. No. Particulars Amount

1. Loss of dependency Rs.16,77,900/-
(Rs.11,750 (income) + Rs.4,700 (40% future prospects) =16,450 x 12 (months) x 17 (multiplier) x  (1/2 deduction)
2. Loss of estate & Funeral Rs. 30,000/-

Thus, the claimants would be entitled to total compensation of Rs.17,47,900/- as against Rs.7,34,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.

16. In the result, we proceed to pass the following:
ORDER a) The above appeal is allowed in part.
b) The impugned judgment and award of the Tribunal is modified to an extent that the claimants are entitled to total compensation Rs.17,47,900/- as against Rs.7,34,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.
c) The enhanced compensation amount will bear interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till date of realization.

d) The respondent-Insurance Company shall deposit the enhanced compensation - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:7539-DB amount with accrued interest before the Tribunal within six weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment.
e) Apportionment, deposit & disbursement of the enhanced compensation shall be made as per the award of the Tribunal.
f) Draw modified award accordingly.
